title: Perfect-input coefficient Hom comparison commutes with etale restriction
statement: Fix a prime l, a finite extension E/Q_l, indices m≤n and the lifted positive-level quotient φ:A→B [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension, def-sf-etale-finite-coefficient-hom-arrow]. Let f:U→T be etale and let K,N lie in the ordinary unbounded derived category of A-module sheaves on T_et [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Assume K is dualizable for its native derived tensor. Then the canonical Hom restriction maps for (K,N) and their scalar extensions are invertible, and the canonical coefficient-Hom comparisons over T and U satisfy exactly LisseHomRestrictionCompatibilityRing [def-sf-finite-free-hom-local-calculation], formed with the specified scalarPullbackIso [def-pur-etale-scalar-pullback-iso]. Both existential arrows are required to equal the published canonical comparisons. There is no boundedness, finite-type or quasi-compactness hypothesis on T,U or N.

proof.text: Derived etale inverse image is strong monoidal [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. The internal-Hom comparison of a strong monoidal functor is invertible on a dualizable first input: identify Hom(K,N) with the dual of K tensor N and transport the exact pairing. Scalar extension is strong monoidal as well, so the reduced first input is dualizable. This proves the two invertibility assertions.

proof.text: Transpose the two sides of the restriction square through the target tensor-Hom adjunction. Evaluation compatibility of the canonical comparison [def-sf-etale-finite-coefficient-hom-arrow], naturality of evaluation in both inputs, and the tensor/unit compatibility of the normalized scalarPullbackIso [def-pur-etale-scalar-pullback-iso] identify both maps with the same restricted reduced evaluation. The normalization is checked on flat-term K-flat representatives, where scalar extension and restriction are the ordinary operations and their balancing maps commute. K-flat resolutions extend it to all derived inputs. Injectivity of transposition proves the exact square.

theorem etalePerfectHomRestriction (T U : Scheme.{u}) (f : U ⟶ T) [Etale f]
    {n m : ℕ} (h : m ≤ n) (K N : finiteHomEtale l E T n)
    (hK : IsDualizable K) :
    ∃ (vT : LisseHomComparisonType
        (ULift.{u + 1, u} (Padic.coefficientExtensionRing l E (n + 1)))
        (ULift.{u + 1, u} (Padic.coefficientExtensionRing l E (m + 1)))
        (finiteHomQuotient l E h) T K N)
      (vU : LisseHomComparisonType
        (ULift.{u + 1, u} (Padic.coefficientExtensionRing l E (n + 1)))
        (ULift.{u + 1, u} (Padic.coefficientExtensionRing l E (m + 1)))
        (finiteHomQuotient l E h) U
        (L(Etale.upperStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1}
          (ULift.{u + 1, u} (Padic.coefficientExtensionRing l E (n + 1)))) f).obj K)
        (L(Etale.upperStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1}
          (ULift.{u + 1, u} (Padic.coefficientExtensionRing l E (n + 1)))) f).obj N)),
      HEq vT (etaleFiniteHomCanonical l E T h K N) ∧
      HEq vU (etaleFiniteHomCanonical l E U h
        (L(Etale.upperStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1}
          (ULift.{u + 1, u} (Padic.coefficientExtensionRing l E (n + 1)))) f).obj K)
        (L(Etale.upperStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1}
          (ULift.{u + 1, u} (Padic.coefficientExtensionRing l E (n + 1)))) f).obj N)) ∧
      LisseHomRestrictionCompatibilityRing _ _ (finiteHomQuotient l E h) T U f
        K N vT vU
